A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching v2 Appendices B–G to v3 Appendices C–H.

before.justification: V2 reports original transformer training experiments, classification evaluations, dataset statistics, and sensitivity analyses in Section 4, Table 1, Figure 1, and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results in Section 4, Table 1, Figure 1, and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, input sequence, attention mask, constrained adversarial pretraining objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged. V3 adds explanations rather than method components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic training distributions, Gaussian test distributions, and MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 binary classification tasks. V3's discussion of filtered natural images introduces no evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons retain standardly and adversarially pretrained transformers, including the strongly adversarial regime in parameter heatmaps. V3 Appendix B discusses task-specific training but adds no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The experimental appendices retain the same preprocessing, training schedules, synthetic sample counts, image class pairs, perturbation budgets, and evaluation procedures. Using theoretically predicted parameters was already disclosed in v2 Appendix C.3; its clarification in v3 Section 4 is not a protocol change.

E4.justification: The same analyses examine perturbation budgets, robust/non-robust/irrelevant dimensions, demonstration counts, learned parameters, and dataset statistics. V3 Appendix B adds conceptual discussion without a new tested ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same means and standard deviations across synthetic batches and the 45 image classification pairs. Repeated-run information and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 values and all six embedded figures are unchanged. For example, both versions report MNIST clean/robust accuracies of 94/4 for the standard model and 93/72 for the adversarial model under the same settings. No experimental result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.2 changes Cov(x_i,x_j) to Cov(yx_i,yx_j), with corresponding corrections in the robustness derivation: v2 Eqs. (A168)–(A174) versus v3 Eqs. (A172)–(A178). Section 3.2 adds epsilon < 1 to the linear-classifier optimum condition. Informal perturbation premises change from epsilon approximately beta to epsilon less than or of order beta. The main theorem forms remain unchanged; the added scalar proof sketch contains a missing overall minus sign in Eq. (A23).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: robust adaptation through clean in-context demonstrations, adaptive emphasis on robust features, the accuracy–robustness trade-off, and larger demonstration requirements.

C2.justification: New Appendix B discusses single-task versus multitask training and the trade-off with task-specific adversarial training. Section 5 explicitly limits the established results to classification and l-infinity perturbations. Section 3.1 replaces the Taylor-law explanation with a moment/tail interpretation, while Section 3.4 qualifies vulnerability beyond the robustness guarantee as potential.

D1.justification: Hardware, optimization settings, preprocessing, and parameter choices are retained in the matched experimental appendices. The repository linked in v3's reproducibility statement was already linked in v2's abstract, so this supplies no new resource or access information.

R1.justification: V3 adds Ruderman (1994) and Srivastava et al. (2003) to motivate natural-image moment assumptions and removes Taylor (1961). The broader related-work coverage and principal novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Extensive copyediting and paragraph revisions span the abstract, introduction, and theoretical discussion. V3 expands assumption explanations and informal theorem summaries, inserts a clarification appendix and illustrative proof sketch, repairs unresolved proof references, and updates publication, affiliation, and funding text. Most existing appendix prose is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves from interrupting the theoretical discussion into the experimental section. Appendix figures are regrouped, with Figure A4 now sharing a page with Figures A2 and A3. Captions and headers receive limited edits; the graphics and table structure remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves the central robustness argument's internal consistency through the covariance corrections, and improves clarity through repaired references and explicit applicability limits. The empirical evidence is unchanged. These gains are tempered by the added sketch's sign error in Eq. (A23) and by unchanged Figure A2 still displaying Cov(x_i,x_j), which does not directly validate the revised Cov(yx_i,yx_j) assumption.
